title: orchestrate lightweight lint-railway and dependency-prune operator
author: Linnea Berg
release_notes:
- Add a lightweight staged lint "railway" to route quick presubmit checks for small changes.
- Introduce dependency-prune operator to collect transitive devdeps and propose staged removal MR candidates.
- Reduce presubmit CI setup time for JS/TS changes by caching language-specific toolchains and fast-failing on syntax errors.
- No runtime or API breaking changes.
body:
Context and motivation:
This PR creates a small, opinionated presubmit path we call the 'lint railway' alongside a dependency-prune operator that automates detection of stale dev dependencies. Motivation: our presubmit latency for small client-side changes has been growing because the monolithic lint runner bootstraps a full toolchain for every PR. Teams want fast feedback for trivial changes and a safe way to reduce devdep churn without manual audits.

Summary of changes (single continuous description):
Implemented a lightweight staged lint router that classifies PRs by footprint (small, medium, large) and routes small changes to an isolated fastpath. The fastpath uses a thin container image and a trimmed lint profile that runs syntax + autofix checks and a subset of ESLint/TS type checks; medium/large changes fallback to the regular lint executor. Added a small Go orchestrator (tools/presubmit/railway) that performs footprint detection using git heuristics, and integrates with existing presubmit metadata. Introduced a Python dependency-prune operator (tools/dep_pruner) which enumerates devdeps from package.json/pyproject, sources recent coverage/hit data, and outputs a ranked pruning proposal (with a JSON report + optional branch creation). Wire-up: updated .github/workflows/presubmit.yml to add new staged lanes, added a feature flag (presubmit.fastpath.enabled) with default true for canary. Also added telemetry hooks to report per-PR presubmit latency and fastpath hit-rate.

Commits (high-level):
- initial: add presubmit railway orchestrator and CI lanes
- add: lightweight container images and trimmed lint profiles
- add: dep_pruner core logic, report generator, and unit tests
- ci: integrate staged lanes into presubmit workflow, feature flag, and telemetry events
- docs: presubmit runbook entry and usage guide for the dep prune proposals
- polish: fix edgecases for binary files and path globs, add more unit tests

Changed areas / notable files (high level):
- .github/workflows/presubmit.yml (add staged fastpath lanes and gating)
- tools/presubmit/railway/main.go (footprint classifier + router)
- images/presubmit/light-lint/Dockerfile (small toolchain image + cache steps)
- tools/dep_pruner/pruner.py (core prune heuristics + report writer)
- tools/dep_pruner/tests/test_pruner.py (unit tests and sample manifests)
- scripts/ci_helpers/cache-warmup.sh (cache warm and fastpath enforcement)
- docs/dev/presubmit-railway.md (how to interpret fastpath results)
- docs/dev/dep-pruner.md (proposal workflow and review guidance)

Checklist: 
- [x] Implement lightweight lint router and container image
- [x] Add dependency-prune operator with report generation
- [x] Integrate new lanes into presubmit CI workflow and telemetry
- [x] Add unit tests for core pruning heuristics and classifier
- [x] Add docs and runbook for on-call and engineering teams

Testing and CI: 
Presubmit workflow ran on a fork with a matrix of small/medium changes. Key checks: 
- presubmit:fastpath (light-lint image) — passed (5/5 runs)
- presubmit:full-lint (standard runner) — passed (2/2 runs; rerun once due to flaky network)
- unit-tests:dep-pruner — passed (coverage 82%)
- e2e:presubmit-integration — passed (smoke only)
One transient failure observed on the full-lint job related to npm registry timeouts; retried automatically and greened. Overall ci_status: pass.

Review conversation (selected highlights, chronological):
Marcus Chen (reviewer) — "Nice direction. The footprint classifier looks promising but please add a defensive timeout when invoking language servers so the fastpath can't hang on weird repos."
Linnea Berg (author) — "Added a 6s timeout and a small metric to surface long-running classifier runs; pushed a follow-up commit."
Sanjay Rao (reviewer) — "Dep-pruner heuristics are good; we should avoid auto-creating branches in org repos. Please make branch creation opt-in with a capability flag and document the safety checks."
Linnea Berg (author) — "Made branch creation opt-in (presubmit.dep_pruner.auto_create_branches=false by default) and added a gating check for org-owned repos; updated docs accordingly."
Evelyn Park (reviewer) — "Can we emit a sparse list of suggested removals to the PR as a comment instead of opening MRs automatically? That will make adoption less intrusive."
Linnea Berg (author) — "Switched default behavior: operator posts a comment with the pruner report and provides an 'Apply proposal' button for maintainers; auto branch creation remains opt-in for teams that opt into an automated cleanup flow."
Marcus Chen (approval) — "Approving after the flag/default changes and tests. Good telemetry added to diagnose regressions."

Design considerations and tradeoffs: 
- Fastpath vs coverage: we intentionally limit the fastpath to syntax/quick checks to ensure near-instant feedback; full-quality checks still run for medium/large PRs and required merges.
- Dep-pruner conservatism: the operator errs on the side of not suggesting removal for deps with recent hits or files matching provided globs. The report includes confidence scores so reviewers can triage.
- Opt-in automation: automatic branch creation is dangerous for org-wide repos; default behavior is non-destructive (PR comment + proposal). Teams can opt-in after review.

Rollout and migration plan: 
- Canary: enable presubmit.fastpath.enabled=true for non-critical repos (ci-sandbox, examples) for 2 weeks.
- Monitor: track fastpath hit rate, false negatives (cases where fastpath missed real issues), and presubmit latency reduction.
- Gradual: extend to client SDK repos if metrics look good, then to core monorepo prefixes.

Observability added: 
- presubmit.latency.fastpath and presubmit.latency.full hashed by repo + PR size category
- dep_pruner.report.generated events with counts and top-10 candidate deps

Risks and mitigations: 
- Risk: fastpath gives false green for subtle type-only regressions. Mitigation: fastpath is a trimmed check only; full check remains blocking on merge. We also added metrics to detect regressions tied to presubmit path.
- Risk: noisy prune proposals. Mitigation: confidence scoring, opt-in application, and human review step described in docs.

Merge outcome: 
- Merge method: squash and merge
- Merge commit summary: "orchestrate: add presubmit lint railway and dep prune operator; wire staged lanes"
- Post-merge followups queued: ENG-2678 (add language-specific heuristics for Rust/Go), ENG-2690 (automated prune MR gating for maintainers)

Notes for on-call: 
- If you see presubmit.fastpath.latency spike (>50th percentile 3x baseline), set presubmit.fastpath.enabled=false via feature flag for the affected repo and notify infra.
- Dep-pruner report failures log to tools/dep_pruner/errors; most failures are network to package registries and will be retried.

If any team wants early access to automated branch creation for dep-pruner, message #dev-infra with the repo list and a short justification.

---
End of PR.
